speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for coming in; I see you are presenting with blisters on your forearm and ulcers on your mucosal surfaces. To help me understand the underlying cause, how long have you noticed these symptoms, and have you experienced any fever, fatigue, or difficulty swallowing?

speaker: Patient
text: 50-year-old female. The patient reports the appearance of blisters on her forearm 3 days ago, accompanied by pain in her left cheek when eating and pain during sexual intercourse for the past week. She has been hiking in the woods recently but denies contact with poison ivy. She has a history of hypertension and osteoarthritis, recently started taking captopril, and discontinued meloxicam 2 weeks ago. Family history includes pernicious anemia and Graves' disease.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Pemphigus Vulgaris. The clinical picture of painful oral and genital ulcers preceded by forearm blisters, combined with recent medication changes (captopril), strongly suggests this autoimmune blistering disorder. I will proceed with ordering specific antibody tests and skin biopsies to confirm the diagnosis. REQUEST TEST: Anti-desmoglein 1 and 2 antibodies. REQUEST TEST: Direct Immunofluorescence. REQUEST IMAGES: Dermatology_flexural_skin_blisters.
